description: This topic examines the general properties of non-metals and explores selected non-metals such as carbon, nitrogen, sulphur and chlorine together with the laboratory preparation, properties, tests, uses and environmental effects of their important compounds.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a general physical property of most non-metals?

options.text: They are good conductors of electricity
They are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity

mcq.explanation: Most non-metals are poor conductors of heat and electricity (graphite is a notable exception), unlike metals which are good conductors, malleable and ductile.

mcq.questionText: Diamond and graphite are both forms of the same element. This phenomenon is called:
mcq.explanation: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different physical forms in the same physical state; diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon.

mcq.questionText: Why is graphite, unlike diamond, able to conduct electricity?

options.text: It contains free ions that move through the structure
Each carbon atom forms four bonds, releasing electrons
Each carbon atom is bonded to only three others, leaving one delocalised electron
It is a metal and all metals conduct electricity

mcq.explanation: In graphite each carbon atom bonds to three others, leaving one delocalised electron per atom free to move between the layers, allowing electrical conduction.

mcq.questionText: Which gas is produced when carbon burns in a limited supply of oxygen?
mcq.explanation: In a limited (insufficient) supply of oxygen, carbon undergoes incomplete combustion forming carbon monoxide (2C + O2 -> 2CO).

mcq.questionText: Which laboratory test confirms the presence of carbon dioxide gas?

options.text: It turns moist red litmus paper blue
It gives a pop sound with a lighted splint

mcq.explanation: Carbon dioxide turns limewater (calcium hydroxide solution) milky due to the formation of insoluble calcium carbonate: CO2 + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCO3 + H2O.

mcq.questionText: Approximately what percentage of the atmosphere by volume is nitrogen gas?
mcq.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere by volume, while oxygen is about 21% and carbon dioxide about 0.03%.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the correct chemical test for ammonia gas?

options.text: It turns moist red litmus paper blue
It gives a pop sound with a burning splint

mcq.explanation: Ammonia is alkaline, so it turns moist red litmus paper blue. It also gives dense white fumes with hydrogen chloride gas.

mcq.questionText: In the laboratory, ammonia gas is usually prepared by heating which mixture?

options.text: Sodium chloride and concentrated sulphuric acid
Ammonium chloride and calcium hydroxide (slaked lime)
Calcium carbonate and dilute hydrochloric acid

mcq.explanation: Ammonia is prepared by heating an ammonium salt with an alkali: 2NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCl2 + 2H2O + 2NH3.

mcq.questionText: Which industrial process is used for the large-scale manufacture of ammonia?
mcq.explanation: The Haber process combines nitrogen and hydrogen (N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3) over an iron catalyst at high pressure and moderate temperature to make ammonia.

mcq.questionText: Sulphuric acid is manufactured industrially by which process?
mcq.explanation: Sulphuric acid is made by the Contact process, in which sulphur dioxide is oxidised to sulphur trioxide over a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst, then absorbed and diluted.

mcq.questionText: When concentrated sulphuric acid is added to blue copper(II) sulphate crystals, the crystals turn white. This shows that concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a:
mcq.explanation: Concentrated sulphuric acid removes the water of crystallisation from hydrated copper(II) sulphate (blue) leaving anhydrous copper(II) sulphate (white), showing it is a dehydrating agent.

mcq.questionText: Which gas is responsible for acid rain and is produced when sulphur burns in air?
mcq.explanation: Sulphur burns in air to form sulphur dioxide (S + O2 -> SO2), a major cause of acid rain when it dissolves in atmospheric moisture.

mcq.questionText: Chlorine gas is collected in the laboratory by:
mcq.explanation: Chlorine is denser than air and soluble in water, so it is collected by downward delivery (upward displacement of air).

mcq.questionText: What is the characteristic effect of chlorine gas on moist litmus paper?

options.text: Turns it red then bleaches it white

mcq.explanation: Chlorine is acidic and a bleaching agent, so it first turns moist litmus red and then bleaches it white.

mcq.questionText: Which one of the following describes a correct trend down Group VII (the halogens) from fluorine to iodine?

options.text: Colour becomes lighter down the group
All halogens are gases at room temperature

mcq.explanation: Down Group VII the halogens become less reactive (fluorine is the most reactive), the colour darkens, and the physical state changes from gas (F2, Cl2) to liquid (Br2) to solid (I2).

fib.questionText: The two main allotropes of carbon studied at O-Level are diamond and _____.
fib.explanation: Diamond and graphite are the two crystalline allotropes of carbon, differing in structure and properties.

fib.questionText: The gas that turns limewater milky is _____.
fib.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with limewater to form insoluble calcium carbonate, producing the milky appearance.

fib.questionText: Carbon _____ is a poisonous gas formed by the incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels.
fib.explanation: Carbon monoxide (CO) is toxic because it combines with haemoglobin and prevents the blood from carrying oxygen.

fib.questionText: In the Haber process, nitrogen reacts with _____ to produce ammonia.
fib.explanation: The Haber process combines nitrogen and hydrogen over an iron catalyst: N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3.

fib.questionText: When ammonia is oxidised industrially in the Ostwald process, the acid produced is _____ acid.
fib.explanation: The Ostwald process oxidises ammonia to make nitric acid (HNO3), which is used to manufacture fertilisers and explosives.

fib.questionText: The process by which nitrogen circulates between the atmosphere, soil and living organisms is called the nitrogen _____.
fib.explanation: The nitrogen cycle describes how nitrogen is fixed, converted into nitrates, used by living things and returned to the atmosphere.

fib.questionText: Sulphuric acid is manufactured industrially by the _____ process.
fib.explanation: The Contact process converts SO2 to SO3 over a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst, which is then used to make sulphuric acid.

fib.questionText: Concentrated sulphuric acid is a powerful _____ agent because it removes water (or the elements of water) from substances.
fib.explanation: Concentrated sulphuric acid dehydrates substances such as sugar and hydrated salts by removing water.

fib.questionText: The greenish-yellow poisonous gas commonly used to disinfect drinking water is _____.
fib.explanation: Chlorine is a greenish-yellow gas widely used to kill bacteria in water treatment and to bleach textiles and paper.

fib.questionText: The acid formed when hydrogen chloride gas dissolves in water is _____ acid.
fib.explanation: Hydrogen chloride gas is very soluble in water and dissolves to form hydrochloric acid (HCl), a strong acid.

tf.questionText: Most non-metals exist as gases or brittle solids at room temperature.
tf.explanation: Many non-metals are gases (oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine) and the solid ones (such as sulphur and iodine) are usually brittle, not malleable.

tf.questionText: Diamond is the hardest naturally occurring substance and is used in cutting and drilling tools.
tf.explanation: Diamond has a giant covalent structure with each carbon bonded to four others, making it extremely hard and suitable for cutting tools.

tf.questionText: Carbon dioxide is a poisonous gas that combines with haemoglobin in the blood.
tf.explanation: It is carbon monoxide, not carbon dioxide, that is poisonous and combines with haemoglobin. Carbon dioxide is not poisonous in normal amounts but can cause suffocation in very high concentrations.

tf.questionText: Ammonia gas is less dense than air and very soluble in water.
tf.explanation: Ammonia is lighter than air and extremely soluble in water, which is shown by the fountain experiment.

tf.questionText: Nitrogen gas is very reactive and burns readily in air.
tf.explanation: Nitrogen is generally unreactive (inert) because of the strong triple bond between its atoms; it does not burn readily in air.

tf.questionText: Sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen are major causes of acid rain.
tf.explanation: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides dissolve in atmospheric water to form acids, causing acid rain that damages buildings, plants and aquatic life.

tf.questionText: Concentrated sulphuric acid is added to water during dilution by pouring the water into the acid.
tf.explanation: For safety, concentrated sulphuric acid must be added slowly to water (not water to acid), because dilution releases a large amount of heat.

tf.questionText: Chlorine can displace bromine from a solution of potassium bromide.
tf.explanation: Chlorine is more reactive than bromine, so it displaces bromine: Cl2 + 2KBr -> 2KCl + Br2.

tf.questionText: Graphite is soft and slippery, which makes it useful as a lubricant and in pencil leads.
tf.explanation: Graphite has layers that slide over one another easily, making it soft, slippery and useful as a lubricant and writing material.

tf.questionText: Nitrates and ammonium salts are important compounds used as fertilisers to supply nitrogen to plants.
tf.explanation: Fertilisers such as ammonium nitrate and ammonium sulphate provide soluble nitrogen that plants need for healthy growth.

summary.questionText: State three general physical properties that distinguish most non-metals from metals.
summary.correctAnswer: Most non-metals are poor conductors of heat and electricity (except graphite), are brittle when solid rather than malleable or ductile, and generally have lower melting and boiling points; many are also gases at room temperature.
summary.explanation: These properties contrast with metals, which are good conductors, malleable, ductile and usually have high melting points.

summary.questionText: Explain why diamond and graphite have very different physical properties even though both are made of carbon.
summary.correctAnswer: In diamond each carbon atom is bonded to four others in a rigid three-dimensional giant structure, making it very hard and a non-conductor; in graphite each carbon is bonded to three others in flat layers held by weak forces, with one delocalised electron per atom, making it soft, slippery and a good conductor of electricity.
summary.explanation: The difference in bonding and structure (allotropy) explains the contrast in hardness, slipperiness and electrical conductivity.

summary.questionText: Describe how carbon dioxide gas can be prepared in the laboratory and tested.
summary.correctAnswer: Carbon dioxide is prepared by reacting calcium carbonate (marble chips) with dilute hydrochloric acid: CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O + CO2. The gas is tested by bubbling it through limewater, which turns milky due to formation of calcium carbonate.
summary.explanation: This is the standard NECTA laboratory preparation and test for carbon dioxide.

summary.questionText: Outline the main stages of the nitrogen cycle.
summary.correctAnswer: Nitrogen is fixed from the air into nitrates by lightning and nitrogen-fixing bacteria; plants absorb nitrates and convert them to proteins; animals eat plants and obtain nitrogen; decomposers break down dead matter and waste releasing ammonia, which is converted by nitrifying bacteria into nitrates, while denitrifying bacteria return nitrogen gas to the atmosphere.
summary.explanation: The nitrogen cycle keeps the amount of nitrogen in the atmosphere and soil balanced through fixation, nitrification and denitrification.

summary.questionText: Describe the laboratory preparation of ammonia gas and how it is dried and collected.
summary.correctAnswer: Ammonia is prepared by heating a mixture of an ammonium salt with an alkali, for example ammonium chloride and calcium hydroxide: 2NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCl2 + 2H2O + 2NH3. The gas is dried using calcium oxide (quicklime) and collected by downward delivery (upward displacement of air) because it is less dense than air.
summary.explanation: Ammonia cannot be dried with concentrated sulphuric acid or calcium chloride because they react with it; quicklime is used instead.

summary.questionText: Give three important uses of ammonia.
summary.correctAnswer: Ammonia is used to manufacture nitrogenous fertilisers such as ammonium nitrate and ammonium sulphate, to make nitric acid (Ostwald process), and as a cleaning agent and in the production of explosives and nylon.
summary.explanation: The largest use of ammonia is in fertiliser manufacture, supporting agriculture and food production.

summary.questionText: Explain why concentrated sulphuric acid is described as a strong acid, a dehydrating agent and an oxidising agent, giving one example of each behaviour.
summary.correctAnswer: As a strong acid it ionises fully in water and reacts with metals and bases (e.g. with zinc to give zinc sulphate and hydrogen). As a dehydrating agent it removes water, turning blue hydrated copper(II) sulphate white or charring sugar to carbon. As an oxidising agent, hot concentrated acid oxidises copper to copper(II) sulphate while being reduced to sulphur dioxide.
summary.explanation: These three roles make sulphuric acid one of the most important industrial chemicals.

summary.questionText: List four major industrial uses of sulphuric acid.
summary.correctAnswer: Sulphuric acid is used to make fertilisers (such as ammonium sulphate and superphosphate), in the manufacture of detergents and paints, in lead-acid car batteries (accumulators), and in the refining of petroleum and the pickling (cleaning) of metals.
summary.explanation: Because of its many uses, the amount of sulphuric acid a country produces is often taken as a measure of its industrial development.

summary.questionText: Describe how chlorine gas is prepared in the laboratory and state one of its tests.
summary.correctAnswer: Chlorine is prepared by warming concentrated hydrochloric acid with an oxidising agent such as manganese(IV) oxide: MnO2 + 4HCl -> MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2. It is collected by downward delivery. It is identified by its greenish-yellow colour and choking smell, and because it turns moist blue litmus paper red then bleaches it white.
summary.explanation: The oxidising agent removes hydrogen from the acid, releasing chlorine gas.

summary.questionText: Explain how sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen cause acid rain and state two harmful effects of acid rain.
summary.correctAnswer: Sulphur dioxide (from burning fossil fuels) and nitrogen oxides (from vehicle engines and lightning) dissolve in rainwater to form sulphurous, sulphuric and nitric acids, producing acid rain. Acid rain corrodes buildings and metal structures, lowers the pH of lakes and rivers killing fish and aquatic life, and damages crops, forests and soil.
summary.explanation: Controlling emissions of these acidic gases reduces acid rain and protects the environment.

hoq.questionText: A student bubbled carbon dioxide gas slowly into limewater. At first the limewater turned milky, but when excess carbon dioxide was passed through, the milkiness disappeared. Which statement best explains this observation?

options.text: The carbon dioxide stopped reacting with the limewater
Insoluble calcium carbonate first formed, then reacted with more CO2 and water to form soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate
The calcium carbonate evaporated as a gas
The limewater was converted back into calcium oxide

hoq.explanation: Excess CO2 converts the insoluble calcium carbonate into soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate: CaCO3 + H2O + CO2 -> Ca(HCO3)2, so the milkiness clears.

hoq.questionText: In the Contact process, the reaction 2SO2 + O2 -> 2SO3 is exothermic and reversible. To obtain a high yield of sulphur trioxide economically, a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst is used at about 450 degrees Celsius and roughly atmospheric pressure. Why is a very high temperature NOT used despite speeding up the reaction?

options.text: A very high temperature would damage the catalyst permanently and stop the reaction
A very high temperature shifts the equilibrium backwards, lowering the yield of SO3 because the forward reaction is exothermic
A very high temperature would convert SO3 directly into sulphuric acid
A very high temperature would make the reaction non-reversible

hoq.explanation: Since the forward reaction is exothermic, increasing temperature favours the reverse reaction and reduces the yield of SO3; about 450 degrees Celsius is a compromise between adequate rate and acceptable yield.

hoq.questionText: A factory wishes to identify an unknown colourless gas. The gas turns moist red litmus paper blue and produces dense white fumes when a glass rod dipped in concentrated hydrochloric acid is held near it. The gas is most likely:
hoq.explanation: Only ammonia is alkaline (turns red litmus blue) and forms dense white fumes of ammonium chloride with hydrogen chloride from concentrated HCl: NH3 + HCl -> NH4Cl.
